answer: Each newcomer squares a group element in a 2048-bit RSA group for 72 sequential hours on one core, seeded by the drand round so nothing can be precomputed. A Wesolowski proof of the result becomes the admission signal, and verifiers check it in milliseconds. Parallel hardware cannot shorten the chain, so 10,000 clones demand 10,000 cores for 72 hours, about 720,000 core-hours or $28,800 at $0.04 each. Every drand round, a zephyr of fresh randomness, expires stockpiled challenges. Ten thousand saplings need ten thousand plots, since no orchard ripens faster by hiring more gardeners.
